::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Feb 12th 1892  
**From:** Elderfield  Otterbourne  Winchester  
**Manuscript:** MS Princeton University, Parrish Collection
:::

Dear Sir
I should think [Miss Knapp](people/person_2110.qmd)’s story would have every chance of attention if you recommended it to [Mr Duncan](people/person_448.qmd) in person, I have always found that literary work stands on its own merits and on the actual opening for it.[^1]

I feel quite sure no recommendation from me would be of half the use of your requesting Canon Duncan to let his reader judge of the M S. That is where the real decision lies, and this is the best time before their number of tales is filled up

Yours truly
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Black-edged paper.
[^2]: Canon Duncan was the secretary of the [National Society](organizations/other_32.qmd) which published stories  for children.
